why: The one narrow opt-out moved onto a CONTAINER, which is the failure mode `forced-color-adjust` invites: the property inherits, so `none` on `.hud-panel` takes every descendant out of colour forcing with it -- the whole interface silently stops honouring the user's high-contrast palette while still passing a rule sweep that only asks whether the declaration exists. Issue #368's boundaries name this explicitly ("No wholesale forced-color-adjust: none") and its criterion 5 requires any use to be narrowly scoped and justified. The swatch is the justified case and the only one: `hud.ts` sets each swatch's fill inline from the palette, so forcing replaces all eleven with a single system colour and the hull and accent pickers stop offering a choice rather than merely looking different. Killed by the guard that asserts `forced-color-adjust` appears exactly once in the whole file AND that its owning selector is `.hud-swatch` -- the count alone would pass this mutation, since it moves the declaration rather than adding one. Scoped to hud.css.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
killedBy: forced-colors conformance (issue #368) opts out of colour forcing in exactly ONE place, and says why
